title: Infrared decision result (engine output)
description: What the engine writes after it prices, checks, scores and ranks the candidates for one project. Every number here is computed by deterministic code from infra.json, forecast.json and catalog.json; no model writes or edits a figure. All money is in EUR. The same inputs give the same file, byte for byte.

schema_version.description: Semver major.minor. Additive changes bump minor; anything that removes/renames/retypes a field bumps major. Readers must accept any 1.x.

inputs.description: Which files this result was computed from.

catalog_illustrative.description: Copied from catalog.json `illustrative`. True means the prices are placeholders and every figure in this file inherits that.

horizon_months.description: Copied from forecast.json; the horizon behind every `horizon_*` figure.

baseline.description: The estate as it is today, before any candidate. The `do_nothing` candidate carries the same estate through the forecast.

violations.description: Hard constraints the current estate already breaks.

candidates.description: Every candidate that was evaluated, `do_nothing` included, feasible or not. Ordered by `rank` (feasible first), then by `violation_distance`, then by `id`.

winner.description: `id` of the winning candidate. Null only when no candidate is feasible; then `closest_if_none_feasible` is set.

closest_if_none_feasible.description: Null when there is a winner. Otherwise the candidate that misses the hard constraints by the least, and what blocks it. The engine never answers 'no result'.

violation_distance.description: Same value as on the candidate.

blocked_by.description: The violations that keep it infeasible, largest distance first.

availability_pct.description: Availability of the critical path, in percent.

confidence.description: The weakest provenance of the inputs behind the figure: observed = high, estimated = medium, synthetic = low.

flags.description: Machine-readable caveats, e.g. `egress_unpriced`, `catalog_illustrative`, `usage_synthetic`, `unpriced_components`. Open list; readers show the ones they know and keep the rest as text.

violation.description: One broken hard constraint, with the component that causes it and how far it is from passing.

constraint.description: Which forecast.json hard constraint. `budget` is `budget.max_monthly_run_cost_eur` (base scenario, horizon month); `migration_budget` is `budget.max_one_off_migration_cost_eur`; `security.<gate>` is one key of `security_gates`.

component.description: infra.json component id that causes the violation. Null when the violation belongs to the whole estate (budget, effort, estate-wide controls).

detail.description: One plain sentence fragment a CTO can read, e.g. 'us-east-1, pii'.

actual.description: What the candidate reaches: EUR, percent or hours for numeric constraints, the offending region or provider for the others. Null when there is nothing to quote.

limit.description: The constraint's limit, in the same unit as `actual`.

distance.description: Normalised shortfall, so that violations of different constraints can be added and the infeasible candidates ranked. Larger is further from passing.

action.description: One change to one component. A candidate with no actions leaves the estate as it is.

delete = remove the resource. stop = keep it but stop paying for compute. resize = change the unit size. scale = change the unit count or the zones. autoscale = turn autoscaling on. move = change the catalog option (provider, product or region). remediate = close a security gate without moving. flag = a finding with no priced change (e.g. a design problem that capacity does not fix).

layer.description: The strategy layer that added this action, e.g. `cleanup_orphans`, `rightsize_in_place`, `security_remediation`. Candidates are cumulative, so a candidate lists the actions of the layers it builds on too.

reason.description: The evidence in one line, e.g. 'gpu_pct avg 0.4, p95 1.0 over 14 d'.

from.description: What the component is today: tier, count, zones or catalog option.

saving_eur_month.description: Run-cost change per month at today's demand. Positive saves money; negative costs more (growing an undersized database, adding a zone). 0 for `flag` and `keep`.

confidence_reason.description: Which input is the weakest, e.g. 'gpu_pct is synthetic'.

run_eur_month_now.description: Run cost per month of the end state at today's demand.

run_eur_month_at_horizon.description: Run cost per month in the horizon month, per scenario. The base value is what the monthly budget is checked against.

horizon_by_scenario.description: Discounted run cost summed over the horizon, per scenario.

migration_eur.description: One-off: effort, running old and new side by side, data-transfer egress.

expected_outage_loss_eur_year.description: (1 - availability) x 8760 x downtime cost per hour.

expected_total_eur.description: Over the horizon: horizon_run_eur + migration_eur + ops + expected outage loss. This is the cost term of the score.

security_remediation.description: The share of this candidate's cost that comes from the `security_remediation` layer, shown apart so the CTO sees what closing the gates costs. Already included in the totals above.

onprem_platform.description: Present when the candidate uses an on-prem platform: the full platform cost per month, allocated by the share of capacity used. Already included in the totals above.

id.description: Unique in the file. Engine strategies use the forecast's strategy names (`do_nothing`, `cleanup_orphans`, ...); candidates proposed by the agent keep the id the agent gave them.

source.description: Who proposed the candidate. Either way the engine priced it.

builds_on.description: `id` of the candidate whose actions this one extends, or null.

violations.description: Hard constraints the end state breaks, largest distance first.

violation_distance.description: Sum of `distance` over the violations. 0 when feasible. Orders the infeasible candidates.

risk.description: Mean catalog risk_factor of the moved components, weighted by their monthly cost. 0 when nothing moves.

payback_months.description: migration_eur / monthly saving against `do_nothing`. Null for `do_nothing` and for a candidate that saves nothing.

score.description: Weighted, min-max normalised (cost, risk, effort); lower is better. Null when infeasible: only feasible candidates are scored.

pareto.description: On the Pareto frontier of (expected total cost, risk, effort) among the feasible candidates. False when infeasible.

rank.description: Final position among the feasible candidates, 1 = winner. Null when infeasible.

rank_by_scenario.description: The rank if only that scenario were to happen. Null when infeasible.

lost_because.description: Null for the winner. Every other candidate says why it lost.

detail.description: One line a CTO can read.

confidence.description: The weakest confidence among the candidate's actions and the baseline pricing.
